title: Observe and causally test whole-brain computation at cellular resolution

concept.text: The innovation would combine simultaneous recording from a substantially complete population of individual neurons across a vertebrate brain with behavioral measurement and precise interventions. Researchers would observe how activity changes across the brain, formulate predictions about how those changes produce particular behaviors, and test those predictions by selectively altering neural activity. The goal is an experimental capability for investigating distributed brain computation; the supplied evidence does not demonstrate its completion.

A wiring map describes anatomical connections but does not directly reveal their changing activity. Activity recordings reveal dynamics, but correlations and sequences alone do not establish which neurons or interactions cause a behavioral outcome. Combining anatomy, cellular activity, behavior and targeted perturbation would connect these different kinds of evidence. In the supplied zebrafish study, observed activity sequences supported hypotheses for subsequent testing through anatomical registration and interventions.

Proposed operational interpretation: cellular resolution should mean that individual recorded neurons can be distinguished and consistently registered, while completeness should refer to a specified neuronal population and denominator. Imaging across most of the brain's volume is a separate accomplishment from recording most of its neurons. Both spatial coverage and neuronal coverage would need explicit reporting.

significance.text: If achieved, this capability would make distributed explanations of perception, decisions and action much more directly testable. Researchers could compare a model's predicted effects of a targeted intervention with the resulting changes in activity throughout the brain and in behavior. That would strengthen mechanistic inference beyond observing which neurons become active together, while also revealing consequences outside the immediately manipulated circuit.

The supplied paper identifies brain-wide state transitions and distributed excitation–inhibition balance as potential applications, and proposes combining voltage imaging with sensory stimulation, fictive behavior and neural perturbation. These are prospective uses of a broader experimental system. The reported imaging result provides a foundation for those experiments, rather than demonstrating their behavioral or causal conclusions.

Conditional synthesis: successful experiments could help distinguish competing accounts of how local circuits participate in a larger computation and constrain future predictive models of brain function. They would not automatically deliver a general theory of cognition or an explanation of subjective experience. Results in larval zebrafish would establish capabilities and mechanisms within that experimental setting; extension to other vertebrates, developmental stages or larger brains would require additional evidence.

missing_breakthrough.text: The missing integrated capability is substantially complete, simultaneous cellular recording during behavior, coupled to interventions specific enough to test predictions about neural dynamics and behavioral outcomes. The supplied study advances the recording component but leaves important parts of this integration for future work. Its animals were paralyzed, behavior was not measured, and the proposed targeted neural perturbations were not demonstrated as part of the reported brain-wide experiment.

The recording challenge combines a three-dimensional field of view spanning the brain, separation of individual cells, timing adequate for millisecond-scale action potentials and sufficient signal fidelity to detect those events. These requirements must be met together. Nominal sampling frequency alone does not establish faithful spike recovery: spike-detection losses, uneven indicator labeling, missed regions and missed cell types can leave important activity unobserved even when the imaging volume is broad.

Motion and intervention compatibility are additional engineering barriers. In the reported experiment, motion artifacts were difficult to correct reliably, prompting the use of a muscle relaxant. A system intended to link activity to behavior must therefore establish recording fidelity under its chosen behavioral conditions. For joint recording and perturbation, the paper proposes spectrally separated voltage indicators and optogenetic actuators, potentially with holographic stimulation; this is a possible technical route, not an accomplished integration in the supplied result.

Scientific synthesis: collecting more signals will not by itself establish a causal explanation. Experiments must define which dynamics and behaviors a proposed mechanism predicts, determine whether the intervention acts on its intended targets, and distinguish those effects from measurement artifacts or other consequences of the intervention. Reliable registration of recorded cells is also needed to connect observations, predictions and manipulations to the same neuronal population.

current_state.text: Wang et al., “Voltage imaging of neurons distributed across entire brains of larval zebrafish,” was published online on August 14, 2026, with DOI 10.1038/s41592-026-03179-7. The supplied review identifies it as a published article and reports brain-wide voltage imaging at 200.8 Hz. Across four analyzed fish, 12,935–19,039 putative neuronal regions of interest remained after artifact exclusion, with reported retention yields of 59–92%. These counts describe retained putative neurons, not a verified census of all neurons in each animal.

The maximum retained count corresponds to approximately one-quarter of a literature estimate of 78,000 neurons in a 7-day-old fish. The imaged animals were 5–6 days old, so the denominator was an estimate from an older developmental stage rather than a matched neuronal count for each specimen. The reported approximately 85% brain-volume coverage must likewise be distinguished from neuronal coverage. The achievement is substantial recording distributed across much of the brain, with incomplete and uneven sampling of its neurons.

The fish were paralyzed to reduce motion to subpixel levels, and the experiment did not include behavioral measurements. Consequently, the observed spontaneous activity sequences could not establish the neurons' functional identities or behavioral relevance. Targeted perturbations, including optogenetics and ablations, were discussed as future ways to test hypotheses. The study therefore did not demonstrate the proposed combination of substantially complete recording, measured behavior and causal intervention.

The supplied peer-review account also distinguishes broad imaging coverage from complete whole-brain neuronal recording. A later reviewer retained that limitation, consistent with the restrained interpretation of the final results. Earlier objections concerned earlier manuscript versions and should not replace the final paper's reported counts or be treated as proof that its limited coverage result is false.

The evidence available through the supplied review is partial. The main HTML and PDF text were truncated; the PDF extraction also warned that some pages lacked extractable text, and no figure inspection was claimed. Nevertheless, the review located explicit textual reports supporting the publication date, retained counts, paralysis and absence of behavioral measurements. The nearly textless MOESM2 extraction could not establish that artifact's identity or supply additional evidence. These access limitations constrain interpretation without negating the supported textual findings.

Evidence-scope limitation: the supplied freshness record contains no searches establishing subsequent developments. The August 2026 demonstration can therefore be described as a documented result, but its status as the latest result, and whether the broader capability remained uncompleted across the field on November 1, 2026, are unresolved. No later achievement or field-wide absence of achievement is inferred here.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: simultaneously record a substantially complete, individually registered neuronal population across the brain of a behaving vertebrate during several prespecified behaviors. Before collecting the decisive evidence, define the neuronal denominator, required coverage, cell-registration standard, behavioral tasks and acceptable recording fidelity. These would be proposed criteria for this innovation, not established community standards.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed demonstration

completion_criteria.text: Proposed causal test: use targeted interventions to produce prespecified changes in neural dynamics and behavior, with prediction tolerances and intervention-specificity requirements defined in advance. Controls should distinguish the intended neural manipulation from optical artifacts and other experimental effects. Independent reproduction should test the causal predictions, rather than merely reproduce a broad imaging field or a similar count of detected cells.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed causal test

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reporting requirements: disclose temporal sampling, spike-detection losses, retained and excluded neuronal candidates, coverage by region and cell type, labeling limitations, registration errors and motion-related losses. Clearly distinguish recorded neurons from the estimated total population and distinguish physical brain-volume coverage from neuronal completeness. Such reporting would address limitations identified in the supplied study, but the particular acceptance thresholds would still need justification.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed reporting requirements

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundary: state the species, developmental stage, preparation, duration, behavioral repertoire and intervention conditions under which the demonstration succeeds. A fictive-behavior preparation should specify what behavioral output it measures and what remains untested. Reproducible performance across several tasks and animals would establish demonstrated breadth within those conditions; finite experiments would not establish literal universality across all behaviors, neurons or vertebrate brains.
completion_criteria.label: Proposed practical boundary

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison with BIO-13, “Establish the physical mechanisms that store and retrieve a long-term memory”: BIO-09 concerns a general capability for observing and perturbing distributed neural computation, whereas BIO-13's title identifies a particular explanatory target—the physical storage and retrieval of long-term memory. BIO-09 could support memory experiments, but a successful recording platform would not itself establish a memory-storage mechanism. This distinction is supported at the level of the supplied titles; BIO-13's full candidate and evidence were not supplied, so its detailed scope remains unverified.

Roster-based comparison with BIO-10, “Observe molecular state and dynamics inside living cells at scale”: both concern measuring changing biological systems, but their stated observational targets differ. BIO-09 focuses on cellular neural activity distributed across a brain and its causal relationship to behavior; BIO-10 focuses on molecular states and dynamics within cells. Molecular measurements could complement brain-wide activity measurements without satisfying BIO-09's behavioral and intervention requirements.

Roster-based comparison with BIO-04, “Create an experimentally predictive virtual cell,” and BIO-14, “Establish causal functions for noncoding elements and poorly understood proteins”: these share an interest in experimentally testable biological explanations. BIO-04 targets predictive modeling at the cell level, while BIO-14 targets causal functions of molecular components. BIO-09 instead proposes an experimental capability at the scale of interacting neuronal populations. These are conceptual connections inferred from the supplied titles, not claims that the other innovations have been achieved or that their detailed requirements coincide.

change_log.change: Preserved BIO-09's identity and expanded its explanation around the distinct roles of anatomy, activity, behavior and intervention.
change_log.reason: The research and review describe a coherent enabling capability whose components answer different scientific questions.

change_log.change: Replaced the shorthand coverage description with the reported sampling rate, four-fish scope, retained ROI range, retention yields and qualified neuronal denominator.
change_log.reason: The review supports these quantitative details and identifies the putative-neuron designation and developmental age mismatch as necessary qualifications.

change_log.change: Separated approximately 85% brain-volume coverage from approximately one-quarter estimated neuronal coverage.
change_log.reason: Broad spatial coverage does not establish neuronal completeness.

change_log.change: Added paralysis, absent behavioral measurements and the prospective status of targeted neural perturbations.
change_log.reason: These limitations explain why the demonstrated imaging result does not complete the proposed innovation.

change_log.change: Expanded the technical barriers to include spike recovery, uneven labeling, motion, registration and compatible recording and perturbation.
change_log.reason: The review supplies useful distinctions that nominal sampling frequency and broad imaging coverage alone would obscure.

change_log.change: Operationalized the completion proposal with prespecified denominators, coverage, registration, prediction tolerances, controls and independent reproduction.
change_log.reason: The earlier terms 'substantially complete' and 'identified' were insufficiently defined; the added requirements remain explicitly proposed.

change_log.change: Preserved conditional significance while limiting claims about cognition, subjective experience and cross-species generalization.
change_log.reason: A powerful experimental platform would strengthen causal tests without automatically resolving those broader questions.

change_log.change: Integrated publication-version context, extraction limitations and the absence of a freshness search.
change_log.reason: Supported textual results should remain usable without implying complete document inspection or knowledge of later field developments.

change_log.change: Qualified the BIO-13 distinction and added title-based connections to other relevant roster entries.
change_log.reason: The roster supports a limited conceptual comparison, but full records for those innovations were not supplied.

unresolved_issues: Whether subsequent work completed the integrated capability, or superseded the August 2026 result, is not established by the supplied freshness record.
The actual neuronal denominator for each imaged 5–6-day-old fish remains unresolved; the reported coverage fraction uses a literature estimate for 7-day-old fish.
No established acceptance thresholds are supplied for substantial completeness, registration quality, spike recovery, intervention specificity or predictive accuracy.

The truncated main texts, PDF extraction warnings and uninspected figures limit verification beyond the explicit passages identified in the review; the nearly textless MOESM2 artifact contributes no usable evidence.

BIO-13's detailed scope and its full boundary with BIO-09 require its complete candidate and evidence. The supplied roster permits only a title-based distinction; detailed comparisons with the other related entries are likewise unverified.
